LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To understand and talk about dates and numbers.
•	 To talk about chores and fun activities.
•	 To understand obligation, lack of obligation, and advice.
MATERIALS
•	 TR#1 Introductions Song
•	 TR#7 After-School Activities Song
•	 TR#9 Prepositions Actions Song
•	 TR#10 Puppy Song
•	 TR#20 Time to Go Home
•	 Calendar (P.E.M.1)
•	 After-School Activities (P.E.M.2)
•	 Days of the Week cards (P.E.M.5)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 2: six sets of Playing cards 
(P.1.2)  
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 4: Fun Activity cards (P.1.2)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 3: Character and Fun Activities 
cards (P.1.2) and Fun Activity/Chores memory cards 
(P.1.1)
•	 Big Book 
•	 Storytelling Pet Care tasks (A3) and Pet playing cards 
(P.S1)
•	 P&P Story 1 Page 5-6 Stickers
•	 Day 3 stickers (1 per child)
•	 Blu-Tack
BEFORE CLASS
P&P S1 | Pages 5&6

•	 Prepare the stickers for pp.5-6 of the student book.
•	 Check the teacher’s dashboard to see if the Ss have 
completed at least half of the recommended activities 
up to this point.
LESSON PLAN
1.– WARM-UP ROUTINES (12’)
•	 Hello + register + booklets
•	 Calendar
•	 After-School Activities, TR#7 (optional)
2.– INTRODUCTIONS SONG (TR#1) (3’)
Get the Ss to stand up and sing the Introductions Song 
following the instructions in the note below.
INTRODUCTIONS SONG
Everywhere we go
People always ask us
Who we are
And where we are from
So we tell them
My name is…
My surname is…
I am from... (x10)
NOTE: this song is recorded with short musical interludes for 
the Ss to take turns introducing themselves. This is repeated 
10 times, but you can stop the song once each S has had a 
turn singing. You can use a toy microphone to get the Ss to 
complete the sentences. They can also sing while clapping 
their hands to the rhythm of “We will rock you”.
3.– ACTIVITY 2: CAN’T/MUST (8’)
P.1.2
P.1.2
P.1.2

> How to Play
Prepare six sets of Playing cards (P.1.2) and place them on 
the table face down in this order:
•	 Character cards (x10: 2 cards per character except 
Grandpa and Grandma)
•	 Red “X” for “can’t” (x10)
•	 Fun Activity cards (x10)
•	 He / She card
•	 Green tick for “must” (x10)
•	 Chores cards (x11)
> Warm-Up
Introduce the activity by saying “Pam, Paul and their family 
want to do their favourite activities, but they can’t! They must 
do their chores first! Look.”
Turn over a card from each pile and form the target structure, 
encouraging the Ss to repeat after you. Emphasise “can’t”, 
“must” and “he/she” so they understand the symbols. Say, 
for example: “Pam can’t listen to music now, she must take 
out the rubbish first.”
> Main Activity
The Ss should take one card from each of the piles mentioned 
above, in the established order, and say, for example, “Grandpa 
can’t play video games, he must take out the rubbish first.”. 
They can either say the phrase as they turn each card or after 
they have turned all five. When a S finishes making the phrase, 
you can keep their pile of cards. 
Each S should make at least one phrase. If you have time, 
you can start again and make new phrases.
NOTE: you can have the Ss make phrases in pairs and reward 
correct phrases with points. You can keep track of them by 
marking the cards with a board marker, or by drawing stars 
next to their name on the board.
> Follow-Up
Once each S has created a phrase, turn over one or two new 
sets of cards and ask them comprehension questions following 
this model: 
•	 “What must Grandpa do?”: encourage the Ss to practise 
using he/she when answering, “He must make the 
bed.” by pointing at the “He/she” cards.
•	 “Can Grandpa play video games?”: encourage the Ss 
to answer “No, he can’t! He must make the bed first.”

4.– STORY WITH CHANGES (PP.2-7) (9’)
Have your Ss choose the storytelling variables and tell them 
the first half of the story. Please see the section on storytelling 
in the Warm-Up routines index.
5.– WORKSHEET: CAN’T/MUST (PP.5-6) (8’)
Can’t / Must

P&P S1 | Pages 5&6
MATERIALS
•	 P&P Story 1 Page 5-6 Stickers
NOTE: if you collected your Ss’ books during the booklet 
activity, have them ask you for it now by saying “Can I have 
my book please?”; otherwise, ask them to take it out of their 
bag. Explain the activity before giving out the books/asking Ss 
to take them out since they might get distracted.
This worksheet shows a chart with the six characters from 
the story as well as a red cross and a green tick with spaces 
underneath for Ss to place stickers.
Before starting, review the names of the different chores 
and fun activities using the P.1.2 cards.
After that, separate the chores and the fun activities cards 
and place them face down on the table in two piles. Ss then 
take turns to pick a card and recite the corresponding target 
language. Have S1 draw a card from the fun activities pile, and 
S2 from the chores pile. For example:
•	 S1 picks “ride a bike”: “Pam can’t ride a bike now...” 
•	 S2 picks “take out the rubbish”: “... she must take out 
the rubbish first.”
Then, all the Ss find the corresponding stickers and place 
them next to the character and under the tick or the cross 
depending on whether they can’t or must do the action.
Continue in this manner until the worksheet has been 
completed.
Upon completion, ask some follow-up questions like: “Can 
Pam ride a bike now?”. Have the Ss answer, “No, she can’t ride 
her bike now; she must take out the rubbish first.”

P&P S1: The Puppy | Day 3
> Scenario A
If your group has achieved the activity goal on My Way (i.e., 
they have done all or most of the activities in the current Mission), 
say, “You’re doing amazing on My Way! You have played lots 
of games in Mission 1, so we can do a special sticker activity 
together!”. Take the Day 3 stickers and have them ask, “Can I 
have some stickers, please?”. Do the activity as instructed below. 
> Scenario B
If your group hasn’t reached the activity goal on My Way, 
simply move on with the class. You will have to complete one 
or two activities from the bonus section to make up for the 
time allotted to this dynamic.
The point of this activity is to review dates in a fun way 
using the sticker pages. The Ss have to place the stickers and 
answer the questions by looking at the calendars. Model the 
task with your Ss by looking for the stickers, placing them, and 
answering the questions. 
Have Ss open p.15 (sticker section) and say, “Let’s find out 
what the date is!”. Point to square number nine and ask, “What

number is this?”. Ss should respond, “It’s number nine!”. Say, 
“Can you find number nine on the sticker sheet?”, and elicit, 
“Here it is!”. Have Ss place the sticker and ask them, “What’s 
the date today?”, eliciting the response “Today is Tuesday the 
10th of January!”.
Continue in the same manner and stick as many stickers 
as time allows. We recommend making this activity more 
dynamic by turning it into a competition as to who can answer 
the questions as fast as possible. You can give points to Ss who 
respond correctly.
KEY (From top to bottom, left to right)
Sticker 9: What’s the date today? Today is Tuesday the 
10th of January.
Sticker 10: What’s the date today? Today is Thursday the 
30th of March.
Sticker 11: What’s the date today? Today is Wednesday 
the 3rd of May.
Sticker 12: What’s the date today? Today is Saturday the 
22nd of July.
Sticker 13: What’s the date today? Today is Sunday the 
26th of August. 
Sticker 14: What’s the date today? Today is Friday the 
1st of September. 
If you can’t finish the whole page, tell the Ss that they can 
continue at home.
8.– ACTIVITY 4: CHARADES (VERSION 2) (7’)
P.1.2
Play the game in the Pictionary style, using the whiteboard. 
A S must take a Fun Activity card (P.1.2.), ask the group “What 
am I doing?”, and draw the action on the board. The rest of the 
Ss try to guess by asking, “Are you watching TV?” to which the 
S must reply, “Yes, I am.” or “No, I’m not.”. To ensure everyone 
gets a turn, set a timer for each round (30 seconds should be 
enough).

If you haven’t done the Group Reward Activity, hand out the 
corresponding stickers (Day 3). If a student is absent, keep 
their stickers and hand them out the following day, together 
with the next sheet.
Remind your Ss to listen to the audio and to do the activities 
on My Way by saying: “It’s very important to be responsible 
and to take care of our pet! So, remember, this week, you 
must listen to the audio every day. You can also play four 
mission games!”.
10.– TIME TO GO HOME (TR#20) (2’)
Sing the Time to Go Home song and have the Ss form a line 
before leaving the class.
BONUS
ACTIVITY 3: GUESSING GAME
P.1.1
P.1.2
P.1.2
> Warm-Up
Place a Character card (P.1.2) on the table and shuffle the 
Fun Activity cards (P.1.2). One at a time, place the Fun Activity 
cards next to the character and ask the Ss: “What is Grandpa/
Pam/etc. doing?”. Encourage them to respond by saying “He/
she’s listening to music.”

> Main Activity
Place one of each of the Fun Activity cards (P.1.1 - without 
chores) face up on the table so the Ss can use them as a visual 
reference. Then put the Character cards (P.1.2) next to the Fun 
Activity cards from Act. 2 (P.1.2) on the table face down.
Model the activity for the Ss. First, take a Character card (P.1.2) 
and place it face up on the table. Then take a Fun Activity card 
(P.1.2) but don’t show it to the Ss. They must guess what the 
character is doing by asking you questions.
So, for example, if you take a Mum card, they should ask, 
“What is Mum doing?” and then gesture to the Fun Activity 
cards (P.1.1) that are face up on the table. The Ss must use 
these cards as a reference to make a guess. The Ss must take 
it in turns to ask, “Is she watching TV?” to which you should 
answer, “No, she isn’t.” or “Yes, she’s watching TV.”
When a S guesses correctly, it’s their turn to take a Character 
card and a new Fun Activity card and repeat the steps above. 
Make sure every S participates at least once.
> Follow-Up
Take a Character card and a Fun Activity card. Ask wrong 
questions on purpose by saying actions that aren’t depicted 
on your card, for example, “Is Dad playing in the park?” to 
which Ss should answer, “No, he isn’t playing in the park. He 
is watching TV.” 
ACTIVITY 9: PREPOSITIONS (TR#9)
> Warm-Up
The Ss should perform the following actions to rehearse 
the movements.
•	 March in line. (all the Ss march in a single file line)
•	 Hide under the table.
•	 Walk next to a friend.
•	 Stand between two chairs.
•	 Jump behind the teacher. (all the Ss jump on the spot 
behind the teacher)
•	 Run in front of the (white) board. (all the Ss run on 
the spot in front of the board)
•	 Sit on a chair.
> Main Activity
Then play the Prepositions Actions Song (TR#9) and dance 
to it.

PREPOSITIONS ACTIONS SONG
(as you sing, simply perform the actions mentioned in the song. 
You can also create a hand choreography for the preposition 
verses.) 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
March in line, in, in line. 
(musical interlude)
Hide under the table, under, under the table.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
Walk next to a friend, next to, next to a friend. 
(musical interlude)
Stand between two chairs, between, between two chairs.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
Jump behind the teacher, behind, behind the teacher. 
(musical interlude)
Run in front of the board, in front of, in front of the board.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
Sit on a chair, on, on a chair. 
(musical interlude)
This is the end, the end, the end.
